Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was very bad for Master students. I didn't got into any of my courses, they spontaneously skipped the classes or switched to Portuguese. From Bachelor it is maybe different but I had a really hard time finding courses and I didn't felt comfortable at all with the classes I was forced to take since there were almost no options for me

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was one day when we signed up for the classes. Because of a technical issue with my account (which was not my fault) I wasn't able to log in and therefore couldn't sign up for anything. The week after I had to walk around with a paper and ask each teacher if they can take me even the classes were full. One professor was so annoyed of the Erasmus students that he consistently talked Portuguese to us eventhough he knew we don't speak Portueguese

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an international office, but they also couldn't really help me cause I didn't really had a choice with the classes at the end

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very unsuccessful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think it is very tricky for a Masters student there because of the limited offer. They should know that they probably won't get any of the classes the university puts on the internet before they decide to go there. I did 2 classes at another faculty (ISEG) and it was way better there but the other classes I had to take at Faculty of Humanities which I couldn't really recommend
